subject.title: fix: block no-auth managed gateway LAN installs

question: Should OpenClaw land this managed install fail-closed preflight for explicit no-auth non-loopback Gateway configs, knowing it changes existing install/refresh behavior before runtime startup?
rationale: Gateway auth mode, bind exposure, service install checks, and upgrade refresh behavior are compatibility- and security-sensitive; the patch is technically clean, but automation should not choose the product/security tradeoff for existing invalid managed installs.

options.title: Accept the earlier install block
options.body: Land the PR as a narrower guard that matches the existing runtime refusal and gives operators remediation before rewriting the managed service.

options.title: Require fuller managed-service proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted Windows Scheduled Task or equivalent managed-service run showing the branch behavior before accepting the compatibility change.

options.title: Pause for broader update proof
options.body: Keep the PR paused if maintainers want the update-mutation claim proven and fixed before adding this narrower install boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept the earlier install block
recommendation.body: Land the PR as a narrower guard that matches the existing runtime refusal and gives operators remediation before rewriting the managed service.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history ties this handle to Gateway auth hardening and adjacent startup/install behavior, making it the strongest available owner for the security-boundary choice.
